observation.description: On the Expo carrier the provider's steady-state connection is broken: the axis reaches 'live' and drops to 'stale' within ~200ms, then reconnects on a ~2s loop indefinitely (witness timeline: live-stale at +0.2s, cycles at 2.4s/6.7s/11.1s...), even while idle. Across cycles the RETAINABLE public query (listSites) blanks permanently after the first cycle (ready/0 on-device while the same query holds 3 rows stable on node) and protected rows blank-then-refill on every cycle, so the UI chips read 'stale' and the sites list is empty in every screenshot - yet second-device commits still deliver in 33-42ms, so the transport works at delivery time. Node control with the SAME two queries against the SAME server holds a stable 'live' connection: the cycling is carrier-specific (suspected: the app-level heartbeat/pong activity accounting or the resume/re-prime path over the memory store misbehaving on RN WebSocket/fetch).
evidence: demos/improvement-sweep/arms/a1-snapback-expo-ios/evidence/shot-02-realtime-after-bob-edit.png (stale chips + empty sites while rows render)

competitorOutcome.description: Firestore RN listeners hold a stable connection on the same simulator class; the frozen 0102 web arms held 'live' steadily on every provider.

mustNotRegress: Delivery latency (33-42ms measured) and the honesty rule that rows are never relabeled live during a gap.
smallestCoherentFix: Diagnose the RN carrier's activity accounting (heartbeat pong receipt) and the retainable resubscribe path after forced reconnect; add an Expo receipt gate asserting a 60s idle hold stays 'live' with public rows intact.
acceptanceWitness: On an Expo simulator, an idle provider with one public and one protected query holds connection 'live' for 60s with rows intact, matching the node control.
